set.body:
Objective:
Build ntab as ScalaFIM's neuroimaging feature-relation layer on top of the independent Frame foundation.

Explicit dependency:
This epic is blocked by the Frame foundation extraction gate. It does not depend on the optional Frame adapters epic, Gale, or DuckDB. The architecture plan may be rebased after the Frame type/API spike, but ntab implementation starts only against stable Frame schemas, expressions, plans, row selections, grouping, and local execution contracts.

Division of responsibility:
Frame owns general scalar relations: runtime and typed schemas, Arrow-compatible scalar columns, expressions, filtering, projection, grouping keys, joins, ordering, optimizer, local engine, and generic source/sink semantics.
ntab owns neuroimaging features: stable feature references, exact volume/surface/parcel support, explicit resolution, feature codecs, support-aware reductions, contributor lineage, drill-down, and leaf domain bridges.
Large images and surface payloads are resolved domain values, not arbitrary Arrow cells. Frame never imports ScalaFIM.

Canonical workflow:
inspect Frame -> bind typed metadata -> filter/group rows in Frame -> bind ntab feature handles -> validate exact support -> resolve selected payloads -> reduce/compare -> inspect receipt -> drill to contributors -> optionally prepare group inference through group-ntab.

Non-negotiable constraints:
- Dynamic schema discovery remains primary; typed evidence is bound at runtime boundaries.
- No implicit resampling, topology correspondence, parcel alignment, or missing-as-NaN policy.
- Metadata operations never trigger feature IO.
- dataset, group, mvpa, multivar, and lower modules do not depend back on ntab; integration bridges are leaves.
- ntab does not recreate Frame's column store, relational IR, optimizer, local engine, or generic IO capability system.

Epic acceptance:
All child gates close; JVM and Scala.js pass the defining workflow; group-ntab proves inferential integration; docs and build edges show the one-way dependency; and Frame remains independently extractable with zero ScalaFIM knowledge.
set.title: Epic: ntab — exact-support neuroimaging feature relations built on Frame
